headline: Civil rights group highlights race-based spirometry and veterans' disability evaluations
dek: The Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law said race-based adjustments in lung function tests may affect how veterans' respiratory disabilities are assessed and compensated.
body:
The Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law said on X, on Veterans Day, that honouring those who served also means ensuring they receive the care, benefits and recognition they have earned.

The organisation pointed to work by Victoria Paul, a Justice Catalyst Fellow at the Lawyers' Committee. According to the post, she examines how race-based medical practices, including race-based spirometry, may affect the way veterans' respiratory disabilities are evaluated and compensated.

The post described spirometry as a common pulmonary function test that measures how much air a person can breathe in and out, and how quickly. It said the test helps assess lung function and identify respiratory conditions. It added that race-based adjustments in these tests have historically determined how lung function is interpreted, potentially affecting access to appropriate care and disability benefits.

The organisation wrote that veterans deserve fair, equitable treatment and called for accountability and "a system that recognizes and protects every veteran". The post did not give further detail on specific policies or data.
key_quote: Veterans deserve fair, equitable treatment—not medical standards shaped by outdated racial assumptions.

source.author_name: Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law
